'''Stephen C. Harvey''' (born 1940) is an American structural biologist with research interest in [[nucleic acid]]s, the [[ribosome]], [[virus]] structure and [[high density lipoprotein]]. He is currently an adjunct professor in the Department of Biochemistry and Biophysics at the [[University of Pennsylvania]] and professor emeritus and [[Georgia Research Alliance]] eminent scholar emeritus in the School of Biology at the [[Georgia Institute of Technology]], [[Atlanta, Georgia]]. Harvey did his undergraduate work at the [[University of California]] (Berkeley), where he received his A.B. degree in physics. In the 1960s, he worked as a rocket test engineer on the [[Apollo program]] (the lunar mission project) and served with the [[Peace Corps]] in [[Colombia]], before entering graduate school in physics at [[Dartmouth College]], where he received his PhD in [[biophysics]] in 1971. Before moving to Georgia Tech in 2003, Harvey was professor in the Department of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics at the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]] (UAB).
 
He is past president of the [[Biophysical Society]] and co-author, with [[J. Andrew McCammon]], of the classic book on [[Molecular Dynamics]], ''Dynamics of Proteins and Nucleic Acids'' ([[Cambridge University Press]], 1987; {{ISBN|9780521356527}}).  Harvey is married to the artist [[Marie Weaver]].  They live in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

The Marie Weaver and Steve Harvey Endowed Scholarship Fund for Graphic Design<ref>"[http://www.uab.edu/art/PDFs/scholarships/UAB_Art_WeaverHarveyScholar.pdf The Marie Weaver and Steve Harvey Endowed Scholarship Fund for Graphic Design]".</ref> was set up in 2003 by the [[University of Alabama at Birmingham]] in honor of associate professor of [[graphic design]] Marie Weaver and her husband, professor of Biochemistry and Molecular Genetics Steve Harvey for their strong support of the arts at UAB.

==Selected publications==

*J.&nbsp;A. McCammon and S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, Dynamics of Proteins and Nucleic Acids (Cambridge University Press, London, 1987).
*S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, "The Scrunchworm Hypothesis: Transitions Between A-DNA and B-DNA Provide the Driving Force for Genome Packaging in Double-Stranded DNA Bacteriophages," J Struct Biol 189:1–8 (2015).
*M.&nbsp;R. Smyda and S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, "The Entropic Cost of Polymer Confinement," J Phys Chem B 116, 10928–10934 (2012).
*S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, A.&nbsp;S. Petrov, B. Devkota and M.&nbsp;B. Boz, "Computational Approaches to Modeling Viral Structure and Assembly," Methods Enzymol 487, 513–543 (2011).
*A.&nbsp;S. Petrov and S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, "Packaging Double-Helical DNA into Viral Capsids: Structures, Forces and Energetics," Biophys J 95, 497–502 (2008).
*J.&nbsp;A. Mears, M.&nbsp;R. Sharma, R.&nbsp;R. Gutell, A.&nbsp;S. McCook, P.&nbsp;E. Richardson, T.&nbsp;R. Caulfield, R.&nbsp;K. Agrawal and S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, "A Structural Model of the Mitochondrial Ribosome," J. Mol. Biol. 358, 193–212 (2006).
*J.&nbsp;P. Segrest, M.&nbsp;K. Jones, A.&nbsp;E. Klon, C.&nbsp;J. Sheldahl and S.&nbsp;C. Harvey, "Apolipoprotein A-I in Discoidal High Density Lipoprotein: A Detailed Molecular Belt Model," J. Biol. Chem. 274, 31755–31758 (1999).
